parts.text: A student is investigating the resistance of a lamp. He is using the circuit shown in Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student connects the crocodile clip on the slide wire to give particular values of the potential difference V across the lamp. He measures the current I in the lamp for each position. Figs. 3.2 to 3.6 show the ammeter readings for values of V = 0.5 V, 1.0 V, 1.5 V, 2.0 V and 2.5 V, respectively. Read, and record in Table 3.1, the value of I for each value of potential difference V . Record each value to 2 significant figures. Fig. 3.2 Fig. 3.3 Fig. 3.4 Fig. 3.5 Fig. 3.6 [2]

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text:
Four correct I values (0.12, 0.15, 0.17, 0.19 and 0.21) present
The fifth one is also correct

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate, and record in Table 3.1, the resistance R of the lamp at each value of V . Use the equation R = V I . [1] Table 3.1 V / V I / A R / Ω 0.5 1.0 1.5 2.0 2.5

ms.label: 3(b)
ms.text: correct calculations of R (4.2, 6.7, 8.8, 10.5, 11.9) or ecf from (a)

parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of R / Ω ( y -axis) against V / V ( x -axis). [4]

parts.text: (e) In this type of experiment, it is possible to change the current and potential difference for the lamp by using a variable resistor rather than a slide wire. On Fig. 3.7, complete the circuit diagram to show a variable resistor used for this purpose. Fig. 3.7 [2]
